t: The first large Thracian state, formed after the Persian retreat from Europe and ruled from the valleys of the Maritsa and Tundzha.
Under Sitalces it reached from the Aegean to the Danube and invaded Macedonia in 429 BCE as an ally of Athens.
Divided after 360 BCE, it fell to Philip II and lived on as a client kingdom until Rome annexed Thrace in 46 CE.
dyk: Thucydides noted that the Odrysians, unlike the Persians, made it a custom to receive gifts rather than give them, so that nothing could be done without one.
ev: Teres I begins to unite the Thracian tribes under the Odrysians
Sitalces becomes an ally of Athens at the start of the Peloponnesian War
Sitalces invades Macedonia with a vast army
Seuthes II hires the survivors of Xenophon’s Ten Thousand
Murder of Cotys I; the kingdom is divided between three rulers
Philip II of Macedon conquers most of the Odrysian lands
Seuthes III builds Seuthopolis near Kazanlak
Claudius annexes Thrace as a Roman province

f.capital: No fixed capital; later Seuthopolis (under Seuthes III)
